'''Joshua Zak''' ({{Langx|he|יהושע זק}}; 26 September 1929 – 14 March 2024) was an Israeli [[theoretical physicist]] and writer known for the [[Zak transform]], [[Zak phase]] and the [[Magnetic Translation Group]]. He received the 2022 [[Israel Prize]] and 2014 [[Wigner medal]].<ref name="technion">{{Cite web|title=Wigner Medal awarded to Professor Joshua Zak - Physics Department, Technion|url=https://phys.technion.ac.il/en/about/news/wigner-medal-awarded-to-professor-joshua-zak|access-date=25 November 2020|website=phys.technion.ac.il}}</ref><ref>Avron J, Bohm A, Schulman LS. The Wigner Medal 2014. In ''Journal of Physics: Conference Series'' 2015 Mar 1 (Vol. 597, No. 1, p. 011004). IOP Publishing.</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
* [[International Colloquium on Group Theoretical Methods in Physics|Wigner Medal]] (2014)<ref name="technion"/>
* [[Israel Prize]], for his achievements in physics (2022)<ref>[http://phys.technion.ac.il/en/about/news/prof-emeritus-joshua-zak-will-be-awarded-the-2022-israel-prize-in-the-field-of-physics-and-chemistry-research Prof. Emeritus Joshua Zak will be awarded the 2022 Israel Prize in the Field of Physics and Chemistry Research]</ref>
* The Brown–Zak [[fermion]] and the [[Zak transform]] are named after him.
